newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE LOCAL TRANCHE SHARES SOAR, FOREIGN FALL.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE LOCAL TRANCHE SHARES SOAR, FOREIGN FALL.

text.p: Buying of local tranches of Singapore blue chip companies pushed several shares to new year highs on Thursday while their respective foreign tranches headed the opposite direction.
Dealers said a "buy local shares and sell foreign theme" seemed to have taken hold as investors speculated that Singapore blue chips might soon do away with a foreign shareholding limit.
Bank stocks and selected blue chips which have foreign tranches saw all their local shares rise while the foreign tranches came under selling pressure.
Total market volume was 96.72 million units with 80 gainers against 231 losers.
DBS and OCBC rose to new year highs of S$9.65 and S$8.35 in the morning session. OCBC foreign touched a new year low of S$13.60 and DBS foreign sank S$1.00 to S$17.80.

"Local fund managers are buying the local tranches as they offer much better value then the foreign shares. But whether the authorities will do away with foreign shares, it is still not clear," said one dealer.
Buying of local shares of index linked stocks like Singapore Press and Singapore Airlines pulled the Straits Times Industrial Index higher to 1,964.73, up 6.11 points, at noon.
Creative Technology led the gainers with a 60-cent rise to S$33.50 while Singapore Press foreign led losers with a S$2 fall to S$26.80.
